ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The electromotive force of the power supply is $E = 32\mathrm{V}$, the internal resistance is $r = 1\Omega$, the fixed resistor is $R = 4\Omega$, and the coil resistance of the motor M is $R' = 3\Omega$. When the switch K is closed and the motor is operating normally, the ideal voltmeter reads $22\mathrm{V}$.

1. What is the mechanical power output of the electric motor?
2. If the motor is stuck and cannot rotate, what is the thermal power of the motor at this time?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The electromotive force of the power supply is $E = 32\mathrm{V}$, the internal resistance is $r = 1\Omega$, the fixed resistor is $R = 4\Omega$, and the coil resistance of the motor M is $R' = 3\Omega$. When the switch K is closed and the motor is operating normally, the ideal voltmeter reads $22\mathrm{V}$. 1. What is the mechanical power output of the electric motor? 2. If the motor is stuck and cannot rotate, what is the thermal power of the motor at this time?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is a power source with electromotive force E and internal resistance r; at the top a fixed resistor R is connected in series; at the bottom there is a switch K. On the right side there is an electric motor M, with coil resistance R' marked beside it. The ideal voltmeter V is connected between the same upper and lower two nodes as the electric motor, therefore it is in parallel with the electric motor, measures the voltage across the electric motor, and does not shunt current. Then reason: When the electric motor operates normally, the voltmeter reading is just the terminal voltage of the electric motor U_M=22 V. The ideal voltmeter has no current, so the main current passes through r, R, and the electric motor. From the loop voltage relation E=I(r+R)+U_M, obtain I=(32-22)/(1+4)=2 A. The input electric power of the electric motor is U_M I=22×2=44 W; the heating power of the coil is I^2R'=2^2×3=12 W. Therefore the mechanical output power P_mech=44-12=32 W. When the electric motor is stuck and cannot rotate, there is no back electromotive force, and the electric motor is only equivalent to the coil resistance R'=3 Ω, connected in series with r=1 Ω and R=4 Ω. The current I=E/(r+R+R')=32/(1+4+3)=4 A. At this time the heating power of the electric motor P_heat=I^2R'=4^2×3=48 W.
